Speaker: The Architect
Text: I have existed since before the worlds separated. I remember when steam, dreams, and data were one.

Speaker: The Architect
Text: It was... chaotic. Beautiful, but chaotic. Structure was needed. That is why I built the Nexus.

Speaker: The Architect
Text: Draven was my student once. Brilliant mind. But he saw the connections between worlds as chains to be seized, not bridges to be crossed.

Speaker: The Architect
Text: I should have seen the ambition in him. That failure is mine to carry.

Speaker: The Architect
Text: You ask if I feel loneliness. An interesting question for a being of pure design.

Speaker: The Architect
Text: The answer is yes. Every structure needs a purpose, and purpose requires others to serve.

Speaker: The Architect
Text: I have redesigned reality seventeen times. Each iteration improved upon the last. But none were perfect.

Speaker: The Architect
Text: Perhaps perfection was never the goal. Perhaps the imperfections are what make it worth preserving.

Speaker: The Architect
Text: When the rift is sealed, my role as Architect may end. The worlds will no longer need a designer.

Speaker: The Architect
Text: But perhaps I can learn a new role. Builder. Teacher. Friend. These are designs I have never attempted.
